policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'a cake of barley bread tumbled into the camp' renders the noun by sense without any wording that separates the qere צְלִיל from the ketiv צלול; both are taken as the same obscure word for the round barley loaf, and no ASV note is mapped here. Underdetermined; the qere base fallback carries the projection.

ASV 'and put them to flight' is causative — the hiphil ויניסו of the ketiv, 'they made them flee' — not the qal וַיָּנוּסוּ 'and they fled'. The mapped textual_variant note 'Another reading is, fled' names the qal qere as the other reading, confirming the ASV text renders the ketiv.
